description: We are NABHYAAN NAVIGATORS, a team driven by curiosity, innovation, and a passion for space exploration. Through NABHYAAN NAVIGATOR, we aim to make lunar landing site planning more accessible through technology, scientific insights, and creative problem-solving. We believe in teamwork, learning, and turning ambitious ideas into meaningful solutions.
summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator, developed by Nabhyaan Navigators, is an interactive lunar mission-planning platform designed to address one of the greatest challenges of lunar South Pole exploration: extreme lighting conditions and limited direct-to-Earth communication opportunities.

Our solution helps mission planners, educators, and space enthusiasts explore potential landing sites and understand how location and mission timing influence operational feasibility. It brings together lunar terrain exploration, celestial positioning, and mission-planning concepts to visualize the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to a selected landing location and its horizon. By examining solar elevation, sunlight availability, terrain-induced shadowing, and potential Earth visibility windows, users can better understand power-generation opportunities and communication constraints.

The project draws upon four authoritative resources: NASA Moon Trek, JPL Horizons System, LROC QuickMap, and the Canadian Space Agency's Moon Exploration portal for scientific context, spatial exploration, and astronomical information.

Our goal is to transform complex lunar mission data into an accessible, intuitive, and comparative experience, helping users evaluate not only where to land on the Moon, but when. Ultimately, the platform aims to support better-informed mission planning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and greater public understanding of sustainable lunar exploration.
details:
NABHYAAN NAVIGATOR

Beyond Horizons. Built for Discovery.

Team Name: NABHYAAN NAVIGATORS
Project: Lunar Landing Site Navigator
Challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
Local Event: Mumbai
Team Members: Vaibhav Gupta (Team Lead) and Sanjyot Parashar (Co-Lead)

1. What exactly does our project do?

NABHYAAN NAVIGATOR is an interactive, web-based lunar landing-site exploration and mission-planning concept developed to address the environmental challenges associated with landing and operating near the Moon's South Pole.

The central idea of our project is simple but important: choosing a lunar landing site is not just about finding the right location; it is also about finding the right time.

The lunar South Pole presents unique challenges because sunlight conditions, terrain visibility, and the apparent position of Earth can change significantly depending on the selected location and time. These factors influence opportunities for solar power generation and potential direct-to-Earth communication.

Our platform aims to bring these interconnected considerations into an accessible visual environment where users can explore lunar locations, understand their environmental conditions, and compare different mission scenarios.

2. Why did we choose this challenge?

We chose the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge because it represents an interesting intersection of space science, engineering, technology, and real-world problem-solving.

The Moon is no longer just an object of scientific curiosity; it is an increasingly important destination for future exploration. However, reaching the lunar surface and operating there safely involves challenges that are very different from those encountered on Earth.

What particularly attracted us to this challenge was the complexity of the lunar South Pole. A location may appear suitable geographically, but its illumination conditions, surrounding crater walls, and Earth visibility can make operations difficult at particular times.

We wanted to explore how such complex scientific information could be transformed into something understandable, visual, and useful.

We also saw an opportunity to create a project that connects astronomical calculations with practical engineering considerations. Rather than simply presenting information about the Moon, we wanted to explore how changing a landing location or mission date could influence the conditions experienced by a lunar mission.

Most importantly, we chose this challenge because it encouraged us to think beyond building an ordinary website. It challenged us to approach a genuine space exploration problem and develop a technology-driven concept around it.

3. How does our project work?

Our project follows a location-and-time-based exploration approach.

A. Lunar landing-site exploration

Users can explore potential lunar landing regions and understand their geographical context. The concept supports examining different locations and comparing the environmental considerations associated with each.

B. Mission date and time exploration

The application emphasizes the importance of selecting an appropriate observation date and time. Since the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth change, different mission schedules can produce different environmental conditions at the same landing location.

C. Solar illumination analysis

Solar elevation relative to the local horizon is an important consideration for lunar surface operations. Our project focuses on explaining how sunlight availability, illumination duration, and terrain obstruction influence opportunities for solar energy generation.

D. Earth visibility and communication analysis

The position of Earth relative to the local horizon is important when considering direct-to-Earth communication. Our concept aims to make potential Earth visibility windows and terrain-related obstructions easier to understand.

E. Terrain exploration

The lunar South Pole contains craters, ridges, slopes, and depressions that can influence local illumination and visibility. Terrain exploration is therefore an important part of understanding potential landing conditions.

F. Scenario comparison

The broader objective is to allow users to investigate how changing a landing location or mission time can affect sunlight availability and potential communication opportunities.

4. What scientific resources do we use?

We selected four NASA and space-agency resources to guide our project.

1. NASA Moon Trek

An interactive lunar exploration resource that helps users understand lunar geography, surface features, craters, and potential landing regions through spatial visualization.

2. JPL Horizons System

An astronomical ephemeris resource that provides information about the positions and motions of celestial bodies. It is relevant to obtaining Sun and Earth position information for selected observation times and locations.

3. LROC QuickMap

A lunar mapping resource that provides access to imagery and available topographic information from lunar observations. It is particularly useful for understanding the complex terrain of the lunar South Pole.

4. Canadian Space Agency — Moon Exploration

An educational resource that provides information about lunar exploration, mission objectives, technologies, and the broader context of human exploration of the Moon.

Together, these resources provide the scientific and educational foundation for our project. Their use in specific calculations or live integrations is dependent on verified data access and implementation.

5. What benefits does our project offer?

Our project aims to provide several benefits:

  • Simplified lunar exploration: Makes lunar geographical and environmental information easier to explore.
  • Location-and-time comparison: Encourages users to examine how mission conditions change with different locations and dates.
  • Better scientific understanding: Connects solar elevation, lunar terrain, illumination, and Earth visibility.
  • Power-generation awareness: Explains why sunlight availability is important for lunar surface operations.
  • Communication awareness: Demonstrates how Earth visibility and terrain obstruction can influence potential communication windows.
  • Educational accessibility: Makes complex astronomical and engineering concepts understandable to students and the general public.
  • Mission-planning foundation: Establishes a framework that can be expanded into a more detailed scenario-comparison and mission-assessment platform.

6. What makes our project creative and innovative?

The creative aspect of NABHYAAN NAVIGATOR lies in combining two important dimensions of lunar mission planning: geographical location and time.

A landing location cannot be evaluated independently of its changing environmental conditions. A site with promising geographical characteristics may experience extended darkness or limited Earth visibility at certain times.

Our project approaches this problem by connecting lunar terrain exploration with celestial positioning and mission timing in a single visual experience.

Instead of treating sunlight, communication, and terrain as separate subjects, we aim to demonstrate how they influence one another.

Our guiding question is:

What if mission planners could explore not just where to land on the Moon, but also when the conditions are most favourable?

This idea forms the foundation of our project.

7. What factors did our team consider?

While developing the concept, we considered several scientific and engineering factors:

  • The Moon's lack of a substantial atmosphere and the absence of familiar atmospheric refraction effects.
  • The influence of local terrain on the visible horizon.
  • Solar azimuth and elevation relative to the landing location.
  • Duration of sunlight and extended periods of darkness.
  • The relationship between sunlight availability and solar power generation.
  • Earth's apparent position and geometric visibility from the lunar surface.
  • Potential direct-to-Earth communication opportunities.
  • Crater rims, ridges, steep slopes, and shadowed regions near the lunar South Pole.
  • Changes in celestial positions over time.
  • The importance of distinguishing geometric visibility from actual operational communication capability.
  • Scientific data quality, calculation assumptions, and validation.
  • The need for an intuitive interface suitable for both technical and non-technical users.

8. What tools and technologies did we use?

Web application development: The web development stack includes TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with React for building interactive user interfaces, Vite for development and building, and Tailwind CSS for responsive styling (subject to verification against the project source).
Lovable was used as a development and prototyping platform to support the creation of our web application.

Scientific and educational resources:

  • NASA Moon Trek.
  • JPL Horizons System.
  • LROC QuickMap.
  • Canadian Space Agency — Moon Exploration.

AI-assisted development and support:

During the development process, we used:

  • ChatGPT by OpenAI.
  • Gemini by Google.
  • Claude by Anthropic.
  • Lovable.

These tools supported brainstorming, research assistance, prompt refinement, coding assistance, debugging, and interface development.

The project idea, challenge selection, overall direction, and design decisions were driven by our team. AI tools served as supporting assistants to help us develop and refine our work. Our team remains responsible for reviewing, testing, verifying, and presenting the final project.

The exact programming languages, frameworks, libraries, and backend technologies are documented separately based on the actual source code rather than assumed.

9. What do we hope to achieve?

Our vision is to make lunar landing-site exploration more understandable, interactive, and accessible.

We hope to develop NABHYAAN NAVIGATOR further into a platform that can support the comparison of multiple landing locations and mission dates using validated astronomical and terrain information.

Future development opportunities include:

  • More detailed lunar terrain visualization.
  • Validated Sun and Earth ephemeris calculations.
  • Terrain-aware horizon and shadow analysis.
  • Illumination and darkness timelines.
  • Potential Earth visibility and communication-window analysis.
  • Simplified solar power and battery assessments.
  • Side-by-side comparison of mission scenarios.
  • Educational explanations of lunar environmental challenges.

Our long-term ambition is to create a bridge between complex scientific information and practical understanding, encouraging more people to engage with the challenges of lunar exploration.

10. Intended impact

NABHYAAN NAVIGATOR aims to contribute to the understanding of one of the most important aspects of future lunar exploration: planning missions around the Moon's unique environmental conditions.

For mission-planning communities, it represents a foundation for exploring location-dependent and time-dependent operational considerations.

For students and educators, it offers an opportunity to understand how astronomy, geography, and engineering come together in space exploration.

For the general public, it provides a way to appreciate why landing on the Moon's South Pole requires careful consideration of sunlight, terrain, and communication.

We believe that making complex scientific concepts more accessible is an important step towards inspiring the next generation of space explorers, scientists, and engineers.

Our Philosophy

NABHYAAN NAVIGATORS

Beyond Horizons. Built for Discovery.

We are not simply exploring a landing location. We are exploring the conditions that make lunar exploration possible.
